status_summary: The Fed's main operative decisions in the period ran opposite to a wind-down. On 2025-10-29 the FOMC announced it would stop reducing its securities holdings on 2025-12-01, and on 2025-12-10 it began reserve management purchases of Treasury bills (from 2025-12-11) to keep reserves ample. Two elements match the chapter: paydowns of agency mortgage-backed securities are reinvested into Treasury bills, so those holdings run off without replacement, and reserve management purchases are limited to Treasury securities. Total assets were about $6.74 trillion on 2026-09-30 (Treasuries $4.56 trillion, mortgage-backed securities $1.90 trillion), compared with the chapter's figure of nearly $9 trillion, and the Fed still pays interest on reserve balances (3.90 percent from 2026-09-17). On 2026-07-09 the Fed announced a balance sheet policy task force; the minutes of the September 2026 meeting, released 2026-10-07, report that the trading desk had paused reserve management purchases and will set their pace month by month to keep reserves ample, and that the Committee reaffirmed its ample-reserves approach, so the framework has not changed toward the recommendation.

timeline.event: FOMC announced it would stop reducing its securities holdings on 2025-12-01, ending the runoff program.

FOMC directed reserve management purchases of Treasury bills (and other Treasuries of three years or less if needed) starting 2025-12-11 to keep reserves ample, and reinvestment of agency securities paydowns into Treasury bills.

Fed announced a Balance Sheet Policy task force (co-led by Karen Dynan, Raghuram Rajan and Jeremy Stein) to assess the costs, benefits and institutional effects of the current approach and report to the FOMC.
Implementation note set interest on reserve balances at 3.90 percent effective 2026-09-17, continued rollover of Treasury principal and reserve management purchases as appropriate.
H.4.1 release of 2026-10-01 shows total assets of about $6.74 trillion, Treasury securities $4.56 trillion, mortgage-backed securities $1.90 trillion and reserve balances $2.95 trillion.

Minutes of the 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-16 FOMC meeting are released. They report that the trading desk had paused reserve management purchases in light of money market conditions and reserve forecasts, that the pace of such purchases is not on a preset course and will be decided monthly to keep reserves ample, that maturing Treasury principal continues to be rolled over and agency principal is reinvested in Treasury bills, and that the Committee reaffirmed its ample-reserves approach.

title: Shrink the Fed balance sheet, hold only Treasuries, and end interest on reserves
uncertainties: The balance sheet size at the start of the period (January 2025) was not verified, so the share of the decline from the chapter's roughly $9 trillion that occurred before 2025 is not stated; the H.4.1 link is the rolling current release and will change. The stage reflects the October 2025 end of runoff and the December 2025 purchases, which run opposite to the chapter's wind-down, while the shift of mortgage paydowns into Treasury bills and the July 2026 task force point partly the other way. The September 2026 minutes do not state when the pause in reserve management purchases began or how long it will last; it is a desk decision within an unchanged ample-reserves framework, not a wind-down, and the standing directive still authorizes such purchases. The Fed press-release index showed no balance sheet announcement between 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-13 (checked 2026-10-13); the next meeting (2026-10-27 to 2026-10-28) falls after the research date.
